task.title: Club news: classes and nesting
task.description: Give two articles the class card, and the third one card featured. Write the rules .card, .card.featured, nav a and ul > li in <style>. No !important, id selectors or style="".

hints: In HTML a class has no dot: <article class="card">.
Two classes separated by a space: class="card featured".
An element with two classes in CSS: .card.featured { ... } - no space.
Links inside the menu: nav a { ... }; direct children: ul > li { ... }.
Do not use !important, # or the style="" attribute.

questions.question: How do you select all elements with the class notice in CSS?
questions.explanation: A class in CSS is written with a dot.

questions.question: Which selector is more specific?
questions.explanation: A class (0-1-0) beats any number of tags.

questions.question: Two rules with the same selector p set different colors. Which one wins?
questions.explanation: With equal specificity the rule lower in the code wins.

questions.question: Which property is NOT inherited?
questions.explanation: Backgrounds, borders and spacing are not inherited.

questions.question: Which notations correctly give an element two classes?
questions.explanation: Classes separated by spaces, no dots, order does not matter.

questions.question: Which questions does the browser use to settle a rule argument?
options: The length of the class name

questions.question: Why is a class better than an id for styling?
options: An id is too strong in rule arguments
An id does not work in CSS
A class is easier to override when needed
questions.explanation: An id works, but it makes styles hard to maintain.

questions.question: Match the selector with what it selects.
questions.explanation: A space, > and + set different relationships.
